text: The diagram shows the process that is used to recycle plastic bottles into new products.

Overall, there are eight stages in the process, which begins with the collection of used bottles and ends with the production of new plastic items. Each stage leads directly to the next, so the process is linear.

First, used bottles are collected, and then they are transported to a recycling plant. At the plant, the bottles are sorted by colour, so that clear and coloured plastic can be treated separately. After that, they are washed, which is the fourth stage of the process. This sorting stage allows the plastic to be separated according to its colour.

Next, the clean bottles are shredded into small flakes. In the sixth stage, these flakes are melted, and the melted plastic is made into pellets. Finally, the pellets are used to make new products. As a result, the plastic from old bottles can be used again instead of being thrown away. The whole process therefore turns waste material into a useful resource.
